1.stem:
Eight symbol-number clusters are given below. Find the three clusters that are exactly identical (including spaces).
A. #4%43@8^7*%$34% 4
B. #4% 43@7^8*%$34%4
C. #4%43@7^7*%$34% 4
D. #4%43@7^7*%$34% 4
E. #4% 43 @7^7*%#34%4
F. #4%43@7^7*%$35% 4
G. #4%53@7^7*%$34%4
H. #4%43@7^7*%$34% 4
1.review: The PDF has inconsistent spaces in ostensibly identical symbol clusters. In this version C, D and H are exact character-for-character matches.
1.explanation: The PDF has inconsistent spaces in ostensibly identical symbol clusters. In this version C, D and H are exact character-for-character matches.

18.stem:
Statement: Children below five years of age should not be assigned lengthy handwriting homework.
Assumptions:
I. Sustained writing may be difficult for some children in this age group.
II. Children in this age group should not be introduced to writing skills at all.
18.review: Removed the explicit “because” clause that effectively supplied assumption I in the question. The revised assumptions distinguish lengthy homework from all early writing instruction. Implicit assumptions should not equate avoiding lengthy homework with being too young to learn any writing. Revised statement makes only assumption I necessary.
18.explanation: Removed the explicit “because” clause that effectively supplied assumption I in the question. The revised assumptions distinguish lengthy homework from all early writing instruction. Implicit assumptions should not equate avoiding lengthy homework with being too young to learn any writing. Revised statement makes only assumption I necessary.

24.stem:
Statement: BEST Bus Travels plans to increase fares by 10%, expecting the change to increase fare revenue.
Assumptions:
1. The price of the ticket is the only consideration in every passenger’s travel decision.
2. The increase in fare per passenger can outweigh any fall in the number of tickets sold.
24.review: The revised premise expects increased total fare revenue, which makes the sufficiency of revenue per passenger relevant. It does not assert that ridership remains unchanged. The fare increase alone does not imply all riders will switch.
24.explanation: The revised premise expects increased total fare revenue, which makes the sufficiency of revenue per passenger relevant. It does not assert that ridership remains unchanged. The fare increase alone does not imply all riders will switch.

32.stem: Which assessment of India’s Sixth Five-Year Plan (1980–85) is best supported by historical economic reviews?
opts: Actual GDP growth exceeded the Plan’s targeted rate, although estimates vary by method
The Plan focused entirely on urban development
All major agricultural crops failed to meet production targets

sources.title: World Bank: Accomplishments of the Sixth Plan

32.review: The PDF falsely suggests Sixth Plan agricultural targets were missed due to famine. Historical evidence indicates foodgrain and oilseed production targets were largely attained.
32.explanation: The PDF falsely suggests Sixth Plan agricultural targets were missed due to famine. Historical evidence indicates foodgrain and oilseed production targets were largely attained.

81.stem:
Change the following indirect speech into the most appropriate direct statement of the coach’s announcement.
Sanvi told Prakash that the coach had announced that practice would be cancelled for the rest of the week because the playing fields were flooded.
opts: “Practice was cancelling for the rest of the week.”
“Practice would have been cancelled for the rest of the week.”
“Practice will be cancelled for the rest of the week.”
“Practice would be cancelling for the rest of the week.”
81.review: The previous corrected stem quoted the correct answer word-for-word. The indirect statement is now the prompt; the candidate must identify the correct direct speech. Quoted nested speech retains would because the original message could already use it. Recast the item to give a unique clear answer.
81.explanation: The previous corrected stem quoted the correct answer word-for-word. The indirect statement is now the prompt; the candidate must identify the correct direct speech. Quoted nested speech retains would because the original message could already use it. Recast the item to give a unique clear answer.

92.stem: Change into passive voice: “Take a pair of binoculars with you; otherwise, you may miss the distant view.”
opts: A pair of binoculars is taking with you; otherwise, the view may miss.
Let binoculars taken with you; otherwise, the view may miss.
A pair of binoculars was taken with you; otherwise, the view would miss.
Let a pair of binoculars be taken with you; otherwise, the distant view may be missed.
92.review: A clearer passive transformation avoids awkward “lest” rephrasing and preserves the modal.
92.explanation: A clearer passive transformation avoids awkward “lest” rephrasing and preserves the modal.

97.stem:
The word “reconnnaissance” in the sentence below is misspelled. Choose its correctly spelled replacement.
“During the preliminary reconnnaissance of the floodplain, the geologists catalogued subterranean fissures and recommended immediate remediation.”
97.review: The publisher’s option A is the correctly spelled replacement; the revised wording makes clear that the choices are possible replacements, not four incorrect words to locate.
97.explanation: Reconnaissance is spelled with one n after “reco” and two consecutive n letters after “co” in the standard form: reconnaissance.
